phpstan-mockery-test.scope: mock(), namedMock(), multi-interface comma syntax, constructor args, Foo[method], makePartial(), shouldAllowMockingProtectedMethods(), allows()/expects() higher-order chains

phpstan-isolated-test.scope: alias: and overload: string mock prefixes

phpstan-bar-test.scope: spy(), shouldReceive(), shouldNotReceive(), shouldHaveReceived(), shouldNotHaveReceived(null), closure argument matchers

psalm-mock-return.scope: Foo[method] partial spec, alias:, overload:, spy(), chained shouldReceive(), allows()/expects() higher-order style

mockery-container.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 Container::parseArguments() and parseStringArgument() target parsing

mockery-mock.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 allows(), expects(), shouldReceive(), shouldNotReceive(), shouldHaveReceived(), shouldNotHaveReceived(), shouldNotHaveBeenCalled(), fluent builders

mockery-composite.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 CompositeExpectation __call forwarding, add(), getMock(), mock(), shouldReceive()

mockery-higher-order.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 HigherOrderMessage::__call() forwarding for expectations and verification

mockery-expectation.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 Expectation builder signatures (andReturnUsing, andReturnValues, andReturnSelf, andReturnArg, andSet, withArgs, withSomeOfArgs)

mockery-matchers.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 static matcher factories (on, capture, subset, type, pattern, ducktype, hasKey, hasValue, any, mustBe, contains)

mockery-phpunit.scope: Mockery 1.6.15 MockeryPHPUnitIntegration trait and MockeryTestCase lifecycle hooks

cases.title: Mock factory methods and helpers return T&MockInterface
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $name): string; } $m = Mockery::mock(Greeter::class); $m->greet('world'); $s = Mockery::spy(Greeter::class); $s->greet('world'); $n = Mockery::namedMock('Alias', Greeter::class); $n->greet('world');
cases.semantics: Mockery::mock(), spy(), namedMock(), instanceMock(), Container::mock(), and the global mock()/spy()/namedMock() helpers return an object satisfying both the mocked class/interface and Mockery\MockInterface.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Infer T&MockInterface for existing classes/interfaces. Report unknown methods on T and reject passing T&MockInterface where an unrelated class is expected.
cases.negative_control: Calling missingMethod() on a Greeter mock or passing a Greeter mock to a parameter expecting ApiClient reports errors; disabling extensions restores missing-method errors on Greeter::greet().

cases.title: Multi-interface specs, comma lists, constructor args, quick definitions, and setup closures
cases.fixture: <?php interface A { public function a(): void; } interface B { public function b(): void; } $m = Mockery::mock(A::class, B::class . ', ' . A::class, [true]); $m->a(); $m->b();
cases.semantics: Container::parseArguments() accepts multiple class-string arguments, comma-separated class/interface strings, constructor argument lists, associative quick-definition maps, and a trailing setup Closure.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Intersect all resolved existing classes/interfaces with MockInterface while ignoring array and closure arguments and deduplicating repeated targets.
cases.negative_control: Disabling extensions loses all target interfaces and produces non-existent-method and invalid-argument diagnostics on MockSpecs.php.

cases.title: alias: and overload: string mock prefixes resolve target class
cases.fixture: <?php final class Api { public function fetch(int $id): string { return ''; } } $a = Mockery::mock('alias:' . Api::class); $o = Mockery::mock('overload:' . Api::class); $a->fetch(1); $o->fetch(2);
cases.semantics: Container::parseStringArgument() strips alias: and overload: prefixes to identify the target class name.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Infer Target&MockInterface when Target exists in the codebase; fall back to MockInterface when Target does not exist.
cases.negative_control: Passing Mockery::mock('overload:' . Greeter::class) into acceptApiClient() reports invalid-argument with Greeter&MockInterface; unknown class overload falls back to MockInterface.

cases.title: Partial mock method list syntax Foo[m1, m2] and Foo[!m1]
cases.fixture: <?php final class Api { public function fetch(int $id): string { return ''; } } $p = Mockery::mock(Api::class . '[fetch]', []); $p->fetch(1);
cases.semantics: Container::parseStringArgument() strips trailing [methodList] (including negated !method entries) to identify the mocked target class without splitting method commas as interfaces.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Infer Target&MockInterface for Foo[m1, m2] and Foo[!m1] specs when Target exists.
cases.negative_control: Calling an unknown method on Mockery::mock(ApiClient::class . '[fetch]') reports non-existent-method on ApiClient.

cases.title: Concrete object partial mocks preserve the wrapped object type
cases.fixture: <?php final class Api { public function fetch(int $id): string { return ''; } } $p = Mockery::mock(new Api()); $p->fetch(1);
cases.semantics: Container::parseArguments() accepts a non-Closure, non-MockConfigurationBuilder object instance and builds a partial mock wrapping it.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Infer ClassName&MockInterface for concrete object arguments while ignoring Closure and MockConfigurationBuilder.
cases.negative_control: Calling an unknown method on Mockery::mock(new GreeterImpl()) reports non-existent-method on GreeterImpl.

cases.title: Expectation builders return CompositeExpectation<Mock> with forwarded signatures
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } $g = Mockery::mock(Greeter::class); $m = $g->shouldReceive('greet')->with('x')->andReturn('hi')->shouldReceive('greet')->andReturnSelf()->getMock(); $m->greet('world');
cases.semantics: shouldReceive(), shouldNotReceive(), allows(string), and expects(string) return a CompositeExpectation wrapping the mock. Forwarded Expectation methods preserve parameter types and return the composite; getMock()/mock() restore the mock type; add() returns void.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Resolve forwarded public Expectation methods with real signatures (including dynamic string args to allows()/expects()), preserve MockType through getMock()/mock(), and keep unknown/invalid-arg/void-chain diagnostics.
cases.negative_control: Unknown method on CompositeExpectation, times('not-an-int'), chaining after add(), and unknown method after getMock() all produce diagnostics.

cases.title: Fluent mock-builder methods preserve T&MockInterface
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } $g = Mockery::mock(Greeter::class)->makePartial()->shouldIgnoreMissing()->shouldAllowMockingProtectedMethods()->byDefault()->allows(['greet' => 'hi']); $g->greet('world');
cases.semantics: makePartial(), shouldIgnoreMissing(), shouldAllowMockingProtectedMethods(), byDefault(), and allows(non-empty-array) return $this at runtime.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Preserve the full receiver intersection T&MockInterface across all fluent mock-builder calls including allows(array) whose interface docblock returns self.
cases.negative_control: Calling unknown methods after makePartial() or allows(['greet' => 'hi']) reports non-existent-method on Greeter.

cases.title: Higher-order expectation chains forward to CompositeExpectation<Mock>
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } $g = Mockery::mock(Greeter::class); $m = $g->shouldReceive()->greet('x')->andReturn('hi')->shouldReceive('greet')->getMock(); $g->allows()->greet('x')->andReturns('hi'); $g->allows([])->greet('x'); $g->expects()->greet('x')->once(); $g->expects(null)->greet('x');
cases.semantics: Zero-argument shouldReceive()/shouldNotReceive()/allows()/expects(), allows([]), and expects(null) return HigherOrderMessage or ExpectsHigherOrderMessage, whose __call forwards to a CompositeExpectation on the mock.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Accept dynamic method calls on HigherOrderMessage/ExpectsHigherOrderMessage and return CompositeExpectation<Mock> so chained shouldReceive() and getMock() retain the mocked type.
cases.negative_control: Calling an unknown method after higher-order getMock() reports non-existent-method on Greeter.

cases.title: Positive verification calls return VerificationDirector directly and via HigherOrderMessage
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } $g = Mockery::spy(Greeter::class); $g->shouldHaveReceived('greet')->with('x')->once(); $g->shouldHaveReceived()->greet('x')->once(); $g->shouldHaveReceived(null)->greet('x')->once(); $g->shouldHaveBeenCalled()->once();
cases.semantics: shouldHaveReceived($method) and shouldHaveBeenCalled() return VerificationDirector; shouldHaveReceived() and shouldHaveReceived(null) return HigherOrderMessage whose forwarded call returns VerificationDirector.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Allow optional/null $method without null-argument or too-few-arguments errors, return VerificationDirector for direct and higher-order calls, and reject Expectation-only methods like andReturn() on VerificationDirector.
cases.negative_control: Calling ->andReturn('hi') after shouldHaveReceived()->greet('x') reports non-existent-method on Mockery\VerificationDirector.

cases.title: Negative verification calls return void/null and reject method chaining
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } $g = Mockery::spy(Greeter::class); $g->shouldNotHaveReceived('greet', ['x']); $g->shouldNotHaveReceived()->greet('x'); $g->shouldNotHaveReceived(null)->greet('x'); $g->shouldNotHaveBeenCalled();
cases.semantics: In Mockery 1.6, shouldNotHaveReceived($method), shouldNotHaveBeenCalled(), and HigherOrderMessage forwarding for shouldNotHaveReceived return null (void), never VerificationDirector.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Return void for direct shouldNotHaveReceived($method), shouldNotHaveBeenCalled(), and forwarded shouldNotHaveReceived()->method() so chaining ->withAnyArgs() or ->once() fails statically.
cases.negative_control: Chaining ->withAnyArgs() on shouldNotHaveReceived('countGreetings'), ->once() on shouldNotHaveBeenCalled(), and ->once() on shouldNotHaveReceived()->greet('x') all report invalid-method-access on void.

cases.title: Expectation and VerificationDirector parameter signatures match runtime rules
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } $g = Mockery::mock(Greeter::class); $g->shouldReceive('greet')->andReturnUsing(static fn (string $n): string => $n)->andReturnValues(['a'])->andReturnSelf()->andReturnArg(0)->andSet('p', 'a', 'b')->withArgs(['x'])->withSomeOfArgs('x');
cases.semantics: Expectation::andReturnArg() rejects negative indexes, Expectation::andSet() accepts variadic mixed values, and VerificationDirector::withArgs() accepts only array or Closure.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Accept valid calls on CompositeExpectation, Expectation, and VerificationDirector while reporting invalid-argument on negative andReturnArg() indexes, non-array/non-Closure withArgs(), and non-array andReturnValues().
cases.negative_control: Negative.php verifies invalid-argument diagnostics for andReturnArg(-1), andReturnValues('not-an-array'), and withArgs(123) on CompositeExpectation, Expectation, and VerificationDirector.

cases.title: Argument matcher factory parameter types and concrete matcher return types
cases.fixture: <?php $on = Mockery::on(static fn (string $s): bool => $s !== ''); $sub = Mockery::subset(['a' => 1]); $typ = Mockery::type('string'); $key = Mockery::hasKey('a');
cases.semantics: Mockery::on(), capture(), subset(), type(), pattern(), ducktype(), hasKey(), hasValue(), any(), mustBe(), and contains() return concrete Mockery\Matcher\* classes and require string/array-key inputs where enforced at runtime.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Preserve concrete Mockery\Matcher\* return types and reject non-Closure arguments to on(), non-array arguments to subset(), non-string arguments to type()/pattern()/ducktype(), and non-array-key arguments to hasKey().
cases.negative_control: Negative.php asserts invalid-argument diagnostics on Mockery::on('not-a-closure'), subset('not-an-array'), type(123), pattern(123), ducktype(123), and hasKey([]).

cases.title: PHPUnit integration initializes properties in MockeryTestCase and MockeryPHPUnitIntegration
cases.fixture: <?php use Mockery\Adapter\Phpunit\MockeryTestCase; final class ExampleTest extends MockeryTestCase { private string $v; protected function mockeryTestSetUp(): void { $this->v = 'ok'; } public function testIt(): void { self::assertSame('ok', $this->v); } }
cases.semantics: MockeryTestCase runs mockeryTestSetUp() from setUp() and MockeryPHPUnitIntegration runs startMockery(), mockeryAssertPostConditions(), and purgeMockeryContainer() around every test.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Treat startMockery(), setUp(), and mockeryTestSetUp() as class initializers on MockeryTestCase subclasses and TestCase classes using MockeryPHPUnitIntegration, and register Mockery lifecycle hooks as entry points.
cases.negative_control: Uninitialized properties on MockeryTestCase subclasses and plain non-Mockery TestCase controls still report uninitialized-property.
cases.versions: Runtime-verified on PHP 8.3, PHPUnit 12.5, Mockery 1.6.15, Mago 1.60.2.

cases.title: Intersection-to-intersection parameter compatibility for mocks
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter {} final class ApiClient {} function take(Greeter&Mockery\MockInterface $g): void {} take(Mockery::mock(ApiClient::class));
cases.semantics: An ApiClient&MockInterface mock does not satisfy a Greeter&MockInterface parameter.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Report invalid-argument when passing ApiClient&MockInterface to Greeter&MockInterface. Confirmed still an upstream Mago 1.60.2 limitation tracked in Negative.php and tests/run.php.
cases.negative_control: IntersectionControl.php confirms plain PHP intersection checking is unaffected; Negative.php pins the known gap count (0) so an upstream Mago fix surfaces immediately.
cases.versions: Confirmed known upstream gap on Mago 1.60.2.

cases.title: Opt-in validation of mocked method names against the target class
cases.fixture: <?php interface Greeter { public function greet(string $n): string; } Mockery::mock(Greeter::class)->shouldReceive('doesNotExist');
cases.semantics: When Mockery's allowMockingNonExistentMethods is disabled, mocking a non-existent method fails at runtime.
cases.analyzer_expectation: When MAGO_MOCKERY_STRICT_METHODS=1 is set, report alfredbez/mockery/unknown-mocked-method for literal method names (and Demeter chain roots or map keys) missing from the mocked target class, while skipping __call/__callStatic/@method/@mixin hierarchies, stdClass intersections, explicit shouldAllowMockingMethod() declarations in scope, dynamic names, and anonymous mocks.
cases.negative_control: Default mode (unset MAGO_MOCKERY_STRICT_METHODS) registers no hook and reports zero issues; strict mode stays silent on valid methods, inherited @method/@mixin/trait __call targets, stdClass intersections, in-scope shouldAllowMockingMethod(), dynamic method names, and anonymous mocks, while still reporting non-allowed methods in the same or another scope.
